subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the square of the length of the subtangent at any point on the curve by² = (x + a)³ varies with the length of the subnormal at that point.

mark_split.label: Find the slope at a general point
Show the ratio is a constant

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.220, chapter 10 APPLICATIONS OF DERIVATIVES, the TANGENTS AND NORMALS sub-section, Short Answer question 8. Chapter 10 is printed as five un-numbered sub-sections inside one chapter box and each sub-section restarts its own numbering, so the sub-section is named here; we ship the whole chapter as ONE unit. ONLY THE QUESTION WAS TAKEN — the solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work, see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. WORDING NOTE, RECORDED NOT SILENTLY CORRECTED: the printed stem says varies WITH the length of the subnormal. The standard meaning in this topic is varies AS, that is, the ratio of the two is a constant, and that is what the working establishes: (subtangent)² = (8b/27) × subnormal. The stem is kept as printed and the answer states the constant explicitly. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the two formulas you use, say where you substitute the curve itself, and say what you have to show at the end.

steps.label: Find the slope at a general point
steps.margin_note: First mark. Work at a general point P(x, y) on the curve, since the question says at ANY point. Implicit differentiation is one line here; making y the subject first brings in a three-halves power.
lines: Let P(x, y) be any point on the curve  by² = (x + a)³,  where a and b are constants.
Differentiate both sides with respect to x:

recall.must_convey: That implicit differentiation of by² = (x + a)³ gives dy/dx = 3(x + a)²/(2by).
accept: differentiate both sides implicitly with respect to x
two b y dy by dx equals three into x plus a whole squared
the slope is three x plus a squared by two b y
implicit ga differentiate chesi m ni rayali
take a general point x comma y on the curve
b is a constant so it stays outside

steps.why: The subtangent and the subnormal both need m at the same general point, so one derivative serves both. Keeping the point general is what makes the final statement true at any point rather than at one.
common_mistakes: Differentiating (x + a)³ as 3(x + a)² without noticing that a is a constant, then adding an extra da/dx term.
Writing 2y instead of 2by on the left.
Taking a numbered point, which proves nothing about ANY point.
steps.memory_tip: One general point, one derivative — both the subtangent and the subnormal are built from the same m.

steps.label: Find the subtangent
steps.margin_note: Second mark. After writing y/m, substitute by² = (x + a)³ into the numerator. That substitution is what collapses the expression to a single bracket.
lines: But by² = (x + a)³ from the curve itself, so

recall.must_convey: That the subtangent y/m becomes 2by²/(3(x+a)²), and using by² = (x+a)³ it simplifies to 2(x + a)/3.
accept: subtangent is y by m
two b y squared by three into x plus a squared
use the curve to replace b y squared with x plus a cubed
curve equation ni substitute chesi simplify cheyyali
the subtangent is two into x plus a by three
one bracket cancels leaving x plus a to the first power

steps.why: The equation of the curve is itself a usable substitution. Replacing by² by (x + a)³ removes both y and b from the subtangent and leaves the simplest possible form.
common_mistakes: Using ym for the subtangent, which is the subnormal.
Cancelling (x + a)³ against (x + a)² to give (x + a)² instead of (x + a).
Leaving the answer as 2by²/(3(x + a)²) without using the curve.
steps.memory_tip: Sub-TANGENT has m underneath. Once it is written, look back at the curve for a substitution that clears the y.

steps.label: Find the subnormal
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Here the y cancels on its own, so no substitution from the curve is needed. Notice that b stays in the answer — it is what makes the constant in the last step.

recall.must_convey: That the subnormal ym = 3(x + a)²/(2b), because the y cancels.
accept: subnormal is y into m
the y cancels straight away
subnormal is three x plus a squared by two b
y cancel ayipoyi three into x plus a square by two b migulutundi
no substitution is needed for the subnormal
b stays in the subnormal

steps.why: The slope has y in its denominator, so multiplying by y removes it at once. The subnormal therefore depends on x and the constants only, which is what the comparison in the next step needs.
common_mistakes: Using y/m for the subnormal, which is the subtangent.
Cancelling the 2b as well as the y.
Squaring the subnormal instead of the subtangent.
steps.memory_tip: Sub-NORMAL multiplies by m, and multiplying by y is what cancels the y sitting under the slope.

steps.label: Show the ratio is a constant
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Varies as means the ratio is free of x and y. Divide the square of the subtangent by the subnormal and show the brackets cancel completely.
lines: This is free of x and y, so it is the same at every point of the curve.

lines.text: ∴ (Subtangent)² = (8b/27) × Subnormal, a constant multiple — so the square of the subtangent varies as the subnormal.

recall.must_convey: That (subtangent)²/subnormal = 8b/27, which is free of x and y, so the square of the subtangent varies as the subnormal.
accept: square the subtangent and divide by the subnormal
the x plus a squared brackets cancel completely
the ratio is eight b by twenty seven
ratio lo x undadu kabatti it is a constant
square of the subtangent is a constant times the subnormal
varies as means the ratio is a constant

steps.why: One quantity varies as another when their ratio is the same at every point. Showing the ratio is 8b/27, with no x and no y left in it, is exactly that statement and is what finishes the proof.
common_mistakes: Comparing the subtangent with the subnormal instead of the SQUARE of the subtangent.
Stopping at the ratio without saying it contains no x or y, which is the point being proved.
Writing (2(x + a)/3)² as 2(x + a)²/9 and forgetting to square the 2.
steps.memory_tip: Varies as means one is a fixed number times the other, so divide and check that every letter except the constants disappears.

insider_note: Form both lengths, then square the subtangent and compare — the question asks for a VARIES relation, not an equality. The constants b and a survive as the factor.
